claims.text: Serum or fingerstick glucose first, to r/o uncontrolled diabetes.
claims.quote: Once excess urine output has been verified by history or measurements, serum or fingerstick glucose determination should be done to rule out uncontrolled diabetes.

claims.text: ⍉hyperglycemia: serum and urine chemistries (lytes, calcium) and serum and urine osmol, sometimes plasma ADH.
claims.quote: If hyperglycemia is not present, then testing is required: Serum and urine chemistries (electrolytes, calcium) Serum and urine osmolality and sometimes plasma antidiuretic hormone (ADH) level

claims.text: Sodium > 142 mEq/L suggests free H2O loss from central or nephrogenic DI; sodium < 137 mEq/L suggests polydipsia.
claims.quote: Hypernatremia (sodium > 142 mEq/L [142 mmol/L]) suggests excess free water loss due to central or nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Hyponatremia (sodium < 137 mEq/L [137 mmol/L]) suggests excess free water intake secondary to polydipsia.

claims.text: Urine osmol < 300 mOsm/kg w H2O diuresis, > 300 mOsm/kg w solute diuresis.
claims.quote: Urine osmolality is typically < 300 mOsm/kg (300 mmol/kg) with water diuresis and > 300 mOsm/kg (300 mmol/kg) with solute diuresis.

claims.text: Still unclear: H2O deprivation test w exogenous ADH, under constant supervision (USU in hsp).
claims.quote: If the diagnosis remains unclear, then measurement of serum and urine sodium and osmolality in response to a water deprivation test and exogenous ADH administration should be done. Because serious dehydration may result from this testing, the test should be done only while patients are under constant supervision; hospitalization is usually required.
In psychogenic polydipsia, urine osmolality is < 100 mOsm/kg (100 mmol/kg).
